meetings.title: 12th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting discussions were carried out regarding 2026 budget proposed by the Ministry of Finance and Planning. 1. South Hithadhoo Constituency member Ibrahim Nazil proposed and South Hulhumale' Constituency member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed seconded to include allocations of 120 million as a subsidy for skipjack tuna fishermen, 165 million as a subsidy for yellowfin tuna fishermen, and 50 million as a subsidy for farmers from proposed special budget as a general recommendation. The proposal was rejected by the majority of members vote. 2. Hanimaadhoo Constituency member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed, and Maradhoo Constituency member Ahmed Didi seconded to include the professional opinion given by MMA Governor as a general recommendation in the report. The proposal was rejected by the majority of members vote. 3. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed, and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to pass total revenue and grants of MVR 40,374,524,647/- (Forty billion three hundred and seventy-four million five hundred and twenty-four thousand six hundred and forty-seven) as proposed by the Ministry of Finance and Planning. In addition, to ensure the strengthening of tax enforcement and the collection of state revenue, the amendments proposed to Act No 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act) are to be passed concurrently with this budget. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 4. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed, and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to pass the 2026 budget for government offices and independent institutions along with the changes proposed by the committee. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 5. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed, and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to pass the "Recurrent Expenditure and Capital Expenditure of Offices 2026" and the "Program Budget of Offices" along with the changes proposed by the committee. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 6. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed, and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to pass the PSIP budget of MVR 8,312,139,881/- (Eight billion three hundred twelve million one hundred thirty-nine thousand eight hundred and eighty-one) proposed by the Ministry of Finance and Planning. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 7. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to add MVR 3,522,176/- (Three Million Five Hundred Twenty Two Thousand One Hundred Seventy Six) to the budget of the People's Majlis, after deducting this amount from the Special Budget, as the amount is less than the budget figure approved by the General Purpose Committee of the People's Majlis. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 8. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed, and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to pass the total budget proposed by the Minister of Finance and Planning for 2026 without any change, but with the amendments to the budget as the budget appropriation structure of the budget has changed. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 9. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed, and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to include as a general recommendation, the construction of an additional government office building to address the shortage of office space faced by government agencies and reduce rent expenditure. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 10. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed, and Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh seconded to pass the 2026 budget proposed by the Ministry of Finance and Planning, along with the changes and recommendations proposed by the committee. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote.

meetings.title: 11th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In this meeting, due to the increasing illegal activities and smuggling in the Customs Controlled Area, discussions were held with officials from Maldives Customs Service and Maldives Ports Limited to gather information about container scanning systems needed by Maldives Customs Service to establish container scanning arrangements at ports to strengthen enforcement measures. Accordingly, Maldives Customs Service informed that once Ministry of Finance and planning provides the budget for the total amount needed to purchase the container scanner and MPL allocates the necessary space at the port for the scanner, the installation work can begin. Although the scanner would be purchased using the Customs budget, ownership would be transferred to MPL. MPL informed that they are considering a mobile solution for the container scanner that can be relocated as needed, and that when the port is relocated to Thilafushi, a modern system with the latest features will be established there. MPL also noted that due to current budget constraints, they are unable to make significant expenditures on this matter at this time. Attendees from Maldives Custome Service: Mr. Ibrahim Mafaaz, Deputy Commissioner of Customs Mr. Ismail Hamdhoon, Assistant Commissioner of Customs Mr. Abdulla Ali, Chief Superintendent Mr. Mumthaz Abdulrasheed, Senior Superintendent Attendees from Maldives Ports Limited: Mr. Hassan Muzni Mohamed, Chief Operations Officer Mr. Mohamed Ameez, Chief Strategy Officer

meetings.title: 10th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In this meeting, discussions were held with officials from the Civil Service Commission regarding the Commission’s proposed budget for 2026. The Commission noted that the budget currently allocated to the commission by the Ministry of Finance and Planning is insufficient to fulfill their responsibilities mandated by Act No 5/2007 (Civil Service Act). In addition, Commission highlighted the need for additional budget to strengthen the administration of the Civil Service Commission, conduct training and professional development programs, inspect and audit civil service institutions, and carry out recruitment for the posts of Secretary Generals and Permanent Secretaries in connection with the local council elections, in addition to conducting induction programs. Attendees from Civil Service Commission for the meeting; Mr. Mohamed Mujuthaz, President of the Commission Mr. Mohamed Nasih, Vice President of the Commission Ms. Fathimath Habeeba, Member of the Commission Dr. Hussain Faiz, Member of the Commission Dr. Deeba Moosa, Member of the Commission Mr. Abdulla Saeed, Secretary General

meetings.title: 9th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In this meeting, the committee met with Governor of the Maldives Monetary Authority regarding the proposed budget for the year 2026, and information was sought about the professional opinion provided by the Governor concerning the budget. In this regard, the Governor provided recommendations on state revenue, expenditure, financing, and medium-term fiscal targets. Additionally, the Governor highlighted that as salaries increase due to pay harmonization, recurrent expenditure will also increase, suggesting that salary increases should be implemented in phases. The Governor also noted that although the energy sector needs development like food security, no work has been done so far to develop this sector. Furthermore, the Governor emphasized that foreign currency issues can only be resolved by increasing reserves. Attendees from Maldives Monetary Authority for the meeting; Ahmed Munawwar, Governor Aishath Asna Hamdhee, Deputy Governor Mariyam Rashfa, Managing Director - Monetary Policy, Economics and Statistics Aminath Shafwath, Executive Director - Monetary Policy and Economics Division

meetings.title: 8th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In this meeting, discussions were held with officials from the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority regarding the Authority’s proposed budget for 2026. The authority highlighted that the biggest challenge they face in achieving their targets in the coming years would be retaining technically qualified staff. Due to higher salaries in the private sector and recent salary increases in other state institutions, MIRA is no longer competitive compared to other independent state institutions in terms of salary, working hours, and restrictions imposed. The authority emphasized that without increasing employee’s salary and improving the work environment, it would be difficult to maintain optimal performance of the organization. In addition, the Authority noted that among the measures to increase state revenue for the year 2026, the full impact of the changes brought to TGST through the amendments to Act No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act), and the changes introduced in 2024 to the Departure Tax and Airport Development Fee will be observed next year. Regarding the budget proposed for 2026, the Committee decided to request the Ministry of Finance and Planning to arrange an additional MVR 4.1 million needed by the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority for staff salaries, training, and programs, without altering the amount. Attendees from Maldives Inland Revenue Authority for the meeting; Mr. Hassan Zareer, Commissioner General of Taxation Ms. Fathimath Ameezah, Deputy Commissioner General of Taxation Mr. Ahmed Shafneez, Director General - Administration and Finance

meetings.title: 7th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the information shared by independent institutions regarding the budget allocated to them in the proposed budget for the year 2026 was reviewed. Accordingly, it was decided to send a letter to the Ministry of Finance and Planning highlighting the following matters as necessary changes to the domestic budget of the offices: The amount requested by the People's Majlis Secretariat to be added to the estimated budget for the year 2026; The amount requested to be added to the Anti-Corruption Commission's estimated budget for 2026 to enhance an and expedite the investigation of major and complex serial corruption cases related to state finances, and to establish forensic resources; The amount requested to be added to the Maldives Customs Service budget to strengthen measures against illegal activities and smuggling in customs-controlled areas, which have been increasing, by establishing container scanning facilities at ports; and The amount requested by the Family Protection Authority to be added to its budget for consultancy and travel expenses; In addition, the Committee also decided to request the Ministry to add the maximum possible amount to the programs requested for budget augmentation by the Civil Service Commission, the Maldives Inland Revenue Authority, the Employment Tribunal, and the Maldives Customs Service. NOTE: Representatives from the budget team of the Ministry of Finance and Planning participated in this meeting. Attendees from Ministry of Finance and Planning for the meeting; Ahmed Saaid Musthafa, Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Adam Badhrullah, Budget Executive Ahmed Azyaan Hameed, Fiscal Analyst Zunain Shareef, Business Planning and Consolidation Consultant

meetings.title: 5th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the Committee met with representatives from Maldives Customs Service regarding the service’s proposed budget for 2026 and gathered information about their budget. The Service noted that the amount allocated to them is MVR 19.3 million less than the budget agreed upon with the Ministry of Finance and Planning, and that this amount is insufficient for fulfilling all the responsibilities and duties mandated by Act No. 8/2011 (Maldives Customs Act) and for the administrative operation of the office. Furthermore, the Service highlighted that additional funds are required beyond the currently budgeted amount to fully discharge Custom's legal obligations and to train staffs. In addition, the Maldives Customs Service noted that to further strengthen the management of Customs Control Areas, they require additional staff to enhance port security, reinforce cargo inspection and clearance processes, increase special operations, and expand enforcement activities. They also highlighted the need for budget allocation to procure container scanning facilities, as well as enforcement and surveillance equipment. meetings.title: 4th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the Committee met with representatives from the Anti-Corruption Commission regarding the commission’s proposed budget for 2026 and gathered information about their budget. It was noted that 78.3% of the Commission's baseline budget for 2026 is allocated for staff salaries and allowances. The Commission highlighted that given limited working space available, they face significant challenges in conducting investigations to fulfill their responsibilities mandated by the Constitution and Article 21 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act. They emphasized that apart from the Maldives Police Service, Anti-Corruption Commission is the main agency conducting criminal investigations in the Maldives. The Commission currently operates in a building where ordinary citizens reside, facing space constraints that hinder their ability to ensure complete security for investigations, for individuals summoned for information gathering, and for strengthening the Commission's overall security measures. Additionally, the Commission mentioned that changes have been implemented in their operational structure to expedite the investigation of cases in 2026. The commission expressed that if their requested budget is approved, it would yield positive results. Due to the lack of necessary investigative resources within the Commission, they often need to seek assistance from the Maldives Police Service, even in cases where allegations are made against the police themselves. Attendees from Anti-Corruption Commission for the meeting; 1. Mr. Adam Shameel, President 2. Mr. Abdulla Nashid, Vice President 3. Mr. Ahmed Nashid, Member 4. Ms. Shiyama Mohamed, Member 5. meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, discussions were held with the Minister of Finance and Planning regarding the proposed budget for the year 2026. During the meeting Minister has clarified information about the budget. In this regard, the Minister highlighted that budget expenditures have been streamlined based on projected revenue, and that a framework will be established in collaboration with State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) and Auditor General to recover outstanding funds due to the government and reduce expenses, implementing a better system than the current system. Furthermore, the Minister also noted that the debt-to-GDP ratio is expected to decrease by 2% by 2028, and the inflation rate is projected to remain at 1.1% in the year 2026. Attendees from Ministry of Finance and Planning for the meeting Mr. Moosa Zameer, Minister of Finance and Planning Mr. Ahmed Saaid Musthafa, Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Mr. Adam Badurulla, Budget Executive Mr. Zunain Shareef, Business Planning and Consolidation Consultant

meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The Committee sat with officials from Auditor General’s Office to discuss the various components proposed in the 2026 budget. The Auditor General emphasized the importance of increasing revenue, recovering outstanding receivables of the government. In addition, Auditor General highlighted implementing projects in priority order to reduce PSIP expenditure, and implementation of pension reforms. Moreover, the Auditor General recommended that the challenges due to the increase in debt will not be eased without reducing expenditure and that the Ministry of Finance and Planning should present to Parliament the measures to reduce expenditure while the budget is passed. Attendees from Auditor General’s Office for the meeting: Mr. Hussain Niyazy, Auditor General Ms. Shirumeena Hussain, Assistant Auditor General Mr. Mohamed Shaan, Director General of Audit Mr. Afzal Hassan, Manager Ms. Hawwa Jannath, Manager

meetings.title: 1st Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: First on the agenda for today’s meeting was the appointment of the Committee chair and Deputy chair of the committee. Shabana Rasheed, Director General, presided over the selection process of committee's chairperson and deputy chairperson. Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh proposed to elect Eydhafushi Constituency member Ahmed Saleem as the Chair of the Committee. It was seconded by Faresmaathodaa Constituency member Ashraf Rasheed and passed unanimously. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh proposed to elect Central Fuvahmulah Constituency member Ali Fazad as the Deputy Chair of the Committee. It was seconded by Faresmaathodaa Constituency member Ashraf Rasheed and passed unanimously. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. Following the election, the Chair of the Committee, Eydhafushi Constituency member Ahmed Saleem presided over and opened the floor to propose the working quorum, voting quorum and the quorum of the committee meetings in which the committee meets with people. Kelaa Constituency member Abdulla Shareef proposed to pass the working quorum as 8 members. It was seconded by Faresmaathodaa Constituency member Ashraf Rasheed and passed unanimously. Furthermore, Kelaa Constituency member Abdulla Shareef proposed to pass the voting quorum as 12 members. It was seconded by Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh and passed unanimously. In addition, Kelaa Constituency member Abdulla Shareef proposed to pass the quorum of the committee meetings in which the committee meets with people as 8 members. It was seconded by Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh and passed unanimously. The voting details for these proposal’s are on “Votes” section of this page. Next on the agenda was the finalizing deadline to complete the work of 2026 Proposed Budget by the committee. Central Fuvahmulah Constituency member Ali Fazad proposed to complete the work of the 2026 Proposed Budget latest by 19 th November 2025. It was seconded by Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdooh and passed unanimously. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. Furthermore, the committee decided to meet with Minister of Finance and Planning and Auditor General regarding the 2026 Proposed Budget on 9 th November 2025. In addition, it was decided to meet with MMA governor on 15 th November 2025. Moreover, the committee decided to send letters to independent institutions to obtain additional information regarding proposed budgets. Also, it was decided to meet with Anti-Corruption Commission and Maldives Customs Service regarding the allocated budget.

meetings.title: 6th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting discussions were carried out regarding 2025 budget proposed by the Ministry of Finance. 1. Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdhooh proposed and Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau seconded to pass total revenue and grants of MVR 39,789,965,227/- (Thirty-nine billion seven hundred and eighty-nine million nine hundred and sixty five thousand two hundred and twenty-seven) as proposed by the Ministry of Finance. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 2. Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdhooh proposed and Kela Constituency member Abdulla Shareef seconded to pass the 2025 budget for government offices and independent institutions as proposed by the Ministry of Finance. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 3. Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdhooh proposed and Kela Constituency member Abdulla Shareef seconded to pass the "Recurrent Expenditure and Capital Expenditure of Offices 2025" report and the "Program Budget of Offices" as proposed by the Ministry of Finance. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. 4. Funadhoo Constituency member Mohamed Mamdhooh proposed and Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau seconded to pass the PSIP budget of MVR 12,378,659,021/- (Twelve billion three hundred seventy eight million six hundred fifty nine thousand twenty one) proposed by the Ministry of Finance. This proposal was passed by the majority of members vote. Next, general recommendations for the 2025 budget was proposed. Dhiggaru Constituency member Ahmed Nazim proposed and North Feydhoo Constituency member Ismail Nizar seconded to include 8 general recommendations. This proposal was passed unanimously. In addition, even though Ministry of Finance initially proposed the total amount of block grant to be issued to the councils as MVR 1,447,316,071/- (One billion four hundred forty seven million three hundred and sixteen thousand and seventy one), it was decided that an additional amount of MVR 699,531,414/- (Six million Ninety Nine Thousand Five Hundred Thirty One Thousand Four Hundred Fourteen) to be provided from the contingency budget as proposed by Ministry of Finance. Dhiggaru Constituency member Ahmed Nazim proposed and Kela Constituency member Abdulla Shareef seconded this proposal and was passed unanimously. Furthermore, Dhiggaru Constituency member Ahmed Nazim proposed to pass the 2025 Budget as proposed by Ministry of Finance along with the changes passed. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau seconded this proposal and was passed by the majority of members vote.

meetings.summary: The committee sat with officials from Ministry of Finance to discuss the budget of the independent institutions proposed in the 2025 budget. In the discussion, the Minister highlighted that the budget of government offices, government ministries and their subordinate offices is proposed to implement government policies. In addition, the Minister highlighted that the budget of independent institutions is determined after consultation with respective institutions and gave assurance that, if any institution finds it difficult to fulfil their mandate with the current proposed budget, the necessary funds will be provided from the contingency budget. meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting discussions were carried out on how to proceed with the review of 2025 budget proposed by the Ministry of Finance. Before the beginning of the review of 2025 State budget, as Central Fuvahmulah Constituency member Ali Fazad and Eydhafushi Constituency member Ahmed Saleem was elected as the chair and deputy chair respectively of the budget committee to review the Supplementary Budget for the year 2024, and since there has been no change in the members and as a short time has passed since the work of Supplementary Budget concluded, whether to re-elect a chair and Deputy chair or commence the review of 2025 budget with the previously elected chair and Deputy chair was opened for discussion. Hanimaadhoo Constituency member Ibrahim Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed to re-elect chair and Deputy chair for the review of 2025 budget. South Hithadhoo Constituency member Ibrahim Nazil seconded the proposal and as no member present at the time objected the proposal, the re-election of the Committee chair and Deputy chair proceeded. Shabana Rasheed, Director General, presided over the selection process of committee's chairperson and vice chairperson. Central Mahchangolhi Constituency member Ahmed Xamyr proposed to elect Central Fuvahmulah Constituency member Ali Fazad as the Chair of the Committee. It was seconded by North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy and passed unanimously. North Thinadhoo Constituency member Saudulla Hilmy proposed to elect Eydhafushi Constituency member Ahmed Saleem as the Deputy Chair of the Committee. It was seconded by Kendhoo Constituency member Mauroof Zakir and passed unanimously. Following the election, the Chair of the Committee, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency member Ali Fazad presided over and opened the floor to propose the quorum (working, voting quorum and the quorum of the committee meetings in which the committee meets with people) or continue with the decision taken regarding quorums on the 1 st meeting of the committee held on 27 th October 2024. Hanimaadhoo Constituency member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed to continue with the former decision taken regarding quorums. It was seconded by South Hithadhoo Constituency member Ibrahim Nazil and passed unanimously. Next on the agenda was finalizing deadline to complete the work of 2025 budget by the committee. Hanimaadhoo Constituency member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed to complete the work of 2025 budget latest by 20 th November 2024. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau seconded the proposal and was passed unanimously. Furthermore, discussions regarding obtaining professional opinion from MMA and Auditor General’s Office and obtaining additional information regarding proposed budgets of independent institutions and individual offices were carried out. Hanimaadhoo Constituency member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed to send letters to the relevant authorities. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau seconded the proposal and was passed unanimously.

meetings.summary: In today’s meeting the committee sat with officials from the Ministry of Finance to clarify the reasonings for the proposed forecasted supplementary budget for the ongoing year 2024, along with officials from Auditor General’s Office to present the office’s professional opinion on the matter. Following the meeting, the committee reviewed the supplementary budget for the year 2024. Maamigili Constituency member Qasim Ibrahim proposed to pass the supplementary budget of MVR 5,119,508,129 (Five Billion one Hundred and Nineteen Million Five Hundred and Eight Thousand One Hundred and Twenty-Nine) as proposed by the Ministry of Finance. This proposal was seconded by Velidhoo Constituency member Mohamed Abbas and passed unanimously by the members participated in the vote.

meetings.title: 1st Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: First on the agenda for today’s meeting was the appointment of the Committee chair and Deputy chair of the committee. Shabana Rasheed, Director General, presided over the selection process of committee's chairperson and vice chairperson. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau proposed to elect Central Fuvahmulah Constituency member Ali Fazad as the Chair of the Committee. It was seconded by Kendhikulhudhoo Constituency member Mohamed Afoo Hamid and passed unanimously. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau proposed to elect Eydhafushi Constituency member Ahmed Saleem as the Deputy Chair of the Committee. It was seconded by Kurendhoo Constituency member Mohamed Shamin Habeeb and passed unanimously. Following the election, the Chair of the Committee, Central Fuvahmulah Constituency member Ali Fazad presided over and opened the floor to propose the working quorum and the quorum of the committee meetings in which the committee meets with people. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau proposed to pass the working quorum of 12 members. It was seconded by Maamigili Constituency member Qasim Ibrahim and passed unanimously. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau also proposed to keep the same quorum for the meetings held by the committee with other people, which was seconded by Velidhoo Constituency member Mohamed Abbas and pass unanimously as well. Next on the agenda was the finalizing deadline to complete the work of supplementary budget by the committee. Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau proposed, and Maamigili Constituency member Qasim Ibrahim seconded to complete the work of the supplementary budget today, 27 th October 2024 and passed by the majority. Furthermore, the committee discussed to formulate a schedule of the work of the committee and pass the supplementary budget. Maamigili Constituency member Qasim Ibrahim proposed against conducting a meeting with Minister of Finance due to the limitation of time, which was seconded by Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau and passed by the majority. However, after further discussions among the members, Baarashu Constituency member Ibrahim Shujau proposed to conduct a meeting with Ministry of Finance, Maldives Monetary Authority and Auditor General’s Office on 28 th October 2024, 14:00 hrs. Kurendhoo Constituency member Mohamed Shamin Habeeb seconded this proposal, and it was passed unanimously. In addition, Hanimaadhoo Constituency Member Abdul Gafoor Moosa proposed and South Hulhumale’ Constituency member Dr. Ahmed Shamheed seconded to request Minister of Finance to present how the budget allocated for the year was incurred till date, during the above-mentioned meeting. However, the proposal was not passed by the committee. Furthermore, as the above-mentioned meeting was scheduled for past the deadline the committee decided on prior, Baarashu Constituency Ibrahim Shujau proposed to revise the deadline and the new deadline as 28 th October 2024. This proposal was seconded by Maamigili Constituency member Qasim Ibrahim and passed by the majority.
